previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a right tibial wound infection following prior ORIF surgery. She underwent irrigation and debridement with primary closure, but due to persistent drainage, a second surgery was performed to place a VAC. Cultures grew Morganella morganii and Enterococcus, prompting antibiotic therapy with meropenem and daptomycin after an adverse reaction to vancomycin. A non-functional PICC line was replaced with a new midline catheter. The wound showed progressive healing with granulation tissue, and the patient remained afebrile and stable. She was anticoagulated for a known DVT, with warfarin dosing adjusted to reach therapeutic INR. She was discharged to extended care on a six-week course of IV meropenem, with instructions for VAC changes, anticoagulation management, and close monitoring for infection recurrence.

limited by a large amount of streak artifact.

bases which is slightly more consolidative appearing at the left base and
could represent atelectasis, but underlying infection should be considered.
Trace left pleural effusion.  Heart and great vessels are unremarkable.  Right
internal jugular central venous catheter terminates in the distal SVC.  No
pericardial effusion.  No pneumothorax.  No axillary or hilar lymphadenopathy

pathologic enlargement.  Airways are patent to the segmental level.

without IV contrast.  Within this limitation, there is fatty infiltration of
the liver.  The gall bladder is surgically absent.  There is fatty atrophy of
the pancreas.  Splenomegaly measuring up to 15 cm is noted.  Bilateral adrenal
glands are unremarkable.  

A 5 mm stone is noted in the left proximal ureter with associated mild
hydronephrosis. Tiny nonobstructing stone in the right renal pelvis. Non-
opacified stomach and intra-abdominal loops of small and large bowel are

enlargement.

FINDINGS:  The study is slightly limited by patient motion.

There is a partially healed fracture of the proximal fibula, with evidence of

There is a lateral fixation plate and screws transfixing a partially healed

The distal tibial diaphyseal fracture is incompletely healed.  There is

lucency within the medullary cavity, surrounded by faint sclerosis, somewhat
fuzzy margins, as well as soft tissue density extending beyond the cortex.

tibiofibular joint with osteophyte formation and sclerosis.  The osseous

concerning for osteomyelitis as described above.

10-25 PMNs and <10 epithelial cells/100X field.  NO MICROORGANISMS SEEN.
NO ACID FAST BACILLI SEEN ON CONCENTRATED SMEAR.

NO OVA AND PARASITES SEEN.  This test does not reliably detect Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora or Microsporidium. While most cases of Giardia are detected by routine O+P, the Giardia antigen test may enhance detection when organisms are rare.
